Here's how I think about using SI (vs AI):

AI has become the umbrella term for nearly everything happening in tech today. That term caught on first. But when you consider what companies like Tesla and SpaceX are ultimately trying to achieve, I think "super intelligence" (SI) is a more accurate description of their ambitions.

At first I thought SI was a silly term to use over AI, but after thinking about it, Tesla and SpaceX are trying to create a real super intelligence, and less so an "artificial intelligence." Think about how we describe someone who's exceptionally smart. We say they're "super intelligent." Nobody says they're "artificially intelligent."

SI would have been a better term from the beginning. A lot of people will probably still call it AI, but Optimus is not going to be artificially intelligent, it's going to have super intelligence. It'll take some getting used to lol

text:
Over long periods of time, debts tend to rise faster than incomes, creating the long-term debt cycle.

Even as people become more indebted, lenders freely extend credit because during economic booms, incomes rise, asset values soar, and the stock market thrives. People borrow more to buy financial assets, pushing prices higher and creating a bubble.

So long as incomes keep rising, the debt burden stays manageable. But this cannot continue forever. Over decades, debt burdens slowly accumulate until debt repayments grow faster than incomes. This forces people to cut back on spending, causing incomes to fall and borrowing to dry up—eventually reversing the entire cycle.

That equation is The Everything Code.

AI and robots change the equation itself. They add workers that dont age, dont retire, get cheaper every year, and add productivity on a scale we've never seen.

By my measurement, the efficiency of intelligence output is doubling roughly every five months. 

This isn't the models getting a bit better... this is the actual amount of intelligence you get out of each unit of energy, doubling, every five months... and the doubling time is shrinking.

Nothing in human history has compounded like this. Not electricity, not the internet. And there's no playbook for it, because every institution we have was built for a world where things changed over decades.

This is what I call The Economic Singularity. Somewhere around 2030 to 2032 the machine economy starts moving faster than the instruments we use to measure it... GDP, earnings, the wage were all built for a world of scarce human labour, all pointed at an economy that no longer runs on it. 

Which means the years between now and then are the window. The whole game is to be positioned on the scarce side of the ledger before the old numbers stop meaning anything, because once the machines are running the machine economy the easy part is over. 

We have maybe five years...

text:
Shocking stat of the day:

US fixed-income ETF trading volume as a % of total ETF volume is up to 27%, its highest in at least 6 years.

This figure has more than doubled over the last several weeks.

By comparison, in June, fixed-income ETFs accounted for just 7% of total ETF volume.

Since 2021, there have been only a couple of brief periods where this figure exceeded 20%.

This comes as the surge in Treasury yields accelerated, with the 10Y Note yield surpassing 5.30% and the 30Y Note yield surpassing 5.60%, both for the first time since 2002.

Investors are capitalizing on the historic moves in the bond market.
